chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) would sometimes feed us al-Farani and al-Akhbisa, then he would feed us bread and oil. So it was said to him, 'If only you would manage your affairs until you equalize it.' He said: 'We manage by the Command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So when He expands for us, we expand, and when He rations for us, we ration accordingly.'

key_terms.الْأَخْبِصَةَ: A type of soft bread or cake
key_terms.الْفَرَانِيَّ: A type of fine bread or pastry

ai.seo_question: How did the Imams manage their household expenses in relation to divine decree?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) practical application of *tadbir* (management), demonstrating that financial prudence is not rigid austerity but a dynamic response to divine decree (*qadr*). By alternating between luxurious foods like *farani* and simple bread with oil, he illustrated the Shia ethical principle of balancing gratitude in prosperity with patience in scarcity, avoiding both extravagance and false poverty. This approach underscores the theological view that human effort in management is subordinate to Allah’s will, a concept deeply rooted in the concept of *al-was' wa al-qabd* (expansion and contraction of provision).

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from one of our companions who said,

en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from certain persons of our people who has said the following:

“Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would feed us milk with sugar or a mixture of dates and bread, then give us bread and oil. It was then said to him (the Imam), ’We wish you organize and plan your affairs to balance them out.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘We do so by the command of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious. When He expands sustenance for us, we also expand spending; and when He gives us in measures, we also spend in measures.”’
